I don't have Claude's reply, but here's why **Haiku 5.5** is the fastest and most efficient model in its family, built for high‑volume, cost‑sensitive work, while its predecessor **Haiku 4.5** already matched Sonnet 4 on coding and agent tasks and scores **73.3 %** on SWE‑bench Verified. It’s available to free, Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise users on Claude.ai and to developers on the Claude Platform, AWS, GCP, and Microsoft Foundry. [1]

For data-center GPUs, NVIDIA’s Blackwell-based platforms like the **H200**, **B200**, and **GB200 NVL72** (alongside the **A100** and **H100**) are engineered for large-scale LLM training and high-density inference. [4] On the consumer side, NVIDIA’s **RTX 5090**, the flagship 5th‑generation card, delivers up to **3,352 TOPS** of INT8 compute and offers a **154 %** performance boost over the RTX 4090 thanks to FP4 precision. [2]

Within Claude Science, over 30 open‑source biomolecular models were accelerated in under four weeks, achieving roughly **4× speedup** on average. [3] These models can cost up to **$10,000** of cloud GPU time per target over a 24‑hour campaign. [6]

A recent deal mentions Anthropic’s TPU but provides no technical details, so its generation or vendor remains unclear. [5]

Many AI teams rely on NVIDIA’s data‑center GPUs for heavy workloads, with the Blackwell and Hopper lines being common. [4]

messages.content: What is the most powerful GPU in the world right now, or TPU, or anything being used for AI? What is Claude using, and what are others using?

The most powerful GPU currently is **NVIDIA H200**, along with its siblings **B200** and **GB200 NVL72**—all Blackwell‑based with HBM3e memory, designed for large‑scale LLM training and high‑density inference. [4] These cards are the standard for large‑scale AI clusters and can handle massive batch sizes with high throughput.  

The top consumer GPU for AI is **NVIDIA RTX 5090**, an Ada‑architecture card that supports FP4 precision and delivers up to 3,352 TOPS of INT8 compute with sparsity. [2][7] It is the best option for users looking to run LLMs and image models locally without a data‑center rig.  

No publicly documented TPU model is identified; **Anthropic's $30B deal** is the only TPU‑related information, and it does not specify a particular TPU generation. [5] This suggests that Anthropic may be using a custom or proprietary TPU solution.  

**Claude** runs its flagship **Haiku 5.5** model on the Claude Platform, available natively and through AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry; **Haiku 5.5** is the fastest and most efficient model in the Claude 5.5 family, built for high‑volume, cost‑sensitive work. [1] Developers can access it via the Claude API or directly on the platform for agent and coding tasks.  

The hardware used by other AI teams is not specified. This means we don't have publicly available data on their specific GPU or TPU choices.
